chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Ibrahim ibn Abi al-Bilad, from Umar ibn Yazeed, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), or he said, to Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him), 'I ask you.' So he said, 'Ask.' I said, 'Why did Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) sell the mothers of the children?' He said, 'For the freeing of their necks [from slavery].' I said, 'And how is that?' He said, 'Any man who buys a slave girl, she bears a child by him, then he does not pay her price, and he does not leave from his wealth what is to be paid off from her, her child is taken from her, and she is sold, so her price is paid.' I said, 'Can they be sold for what is besides that, from the avenues of debt and its various forms?' He said, 'No.'

key_terms.أُمَّهَاتِ الْأَوْلَادِ: Mothers of the children (slave women who bore children by their masters)

ai.seo_question: Why did Imam Ali sell the mothers of his children and what is the specific legal condition for their sale?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the specific legal mechanism of 'fakk al-raqabah' (freeing the neck) applied by Imam Ali (AS), distinguishing the sale of Ummahat al-Awlad for debt repayment from general commercial transactions. Scholarly context highlights that this ruling prevents the indefinite enslavement of mothers due to unpaid purchase prices, ensuring their liberation through the sale of their offspring, a practice rooted in pre-Islamic and early Islamic jurisprudence. It underscores the principle that this specific category of slaves is sold exclusively for ransom and not for other types of debts, preserving their status as mothers of the faithful.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Ibrahim Bin Abu Al Balaad, from Umar Bin Yazeed who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>’, or said, ‘Abu Ibrahim<sup>asws</sup> (7<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>), ‘I would like to ask you<sup>asws</sup>’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Ask’. So I said, ‘Why did Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> sell the mother of the children?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Regarding their escape from slavery’. I said, ‘And how was that?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Whichever man buys a slave girl, so she begets, then her price is not paid, and he does not leave from the wealth what is to be paid off from her, her child would be taken from her, and it would be sold, so her price would be paid’. I said, ‘Can he sell regarding what is beside that from the matter of the debts and its aspects?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said; ‘No’.
